new_pages.title: SCORING
new_pages.body:
SCORING

THREE BOXES. TWO FILL A DAY. GOOD IS MANDATORY.

GOOD - every drill you ran has a mark, and at least one mark is a plus or a minus.
BAG - your missed line is at or under the pass line printed on that page.
FINISH - the racks line and the free throw line are both met.

W is a win. Two of three, and GOOD has to be one of them.
P is a perfect day. All three boxes and a level moved today.
A dash is fewer than two boxes, or GOOD missing.
S is a game, travel or sick day. Not a win. Does not break the streak.

Vitamins is not a box. It is the price of entry. You do it, it is not scored, and it never pads your streak.

TUESDAY IS ITS OWN DAY. Practice eats the afternoon, so BAG and FINISH do not exist. Tuesday is GOOD and the Closer. Both, or the day is a dash. That is the whole Tuesday score.

WHY GOOD CANNOT BE BOUGHT OFF
You cannot honestly score a constraint drill on makes. A make count on a deliberately awkward rep pays you to make it less awkward. So GOOD is not scored on outcome. It gets a veto instead. You can run a clean bag block and shoot 46 free throws and still log a dash if you cruised through your Good page.
An all equals day is cruising. It fails GOOD. At least one drill has to get pushed to the edge, and the only way to find an edge is to go over it once.

WHY A PLUS IS NOT A BRAG
A plus is a bill. It makes tomorrow harder, automatically, overnight, and you have to run that harder level in the morning. A minus costs you nothing and is the most useful thing you can write. There is no reason to lie in either direction, which is exactly what a make count on an awkward rep could never say.

WHY EVERYTHING TIGHTENS
Three passes in a row on any line and the line tightens. Two fails and it loosens one. Same rule on the Good levels, the bag pass lines and the 50/50 lines, so there is one rule to remember instead of three. You never work any of it out. The number printed on the page is always the current number.

WHAT YOU NEVER DO
You never fill in a log table. Not one, not ever, not as a backup if the sync is late. If the sync is late the row gets written late.
You never edit a line that is already on a page. Everything you type is a new line at the bottom with today's date in front of it.
You never add anything up. Not racks, not makes, not days at a level.

WHAT THE DAY COSTS
About thirty to forty seconds, across four moments, none of them longer than twelve seconds.
A clean bag day costs zero keystrokes. The better you get, the less you type. Every other logging system you have ever used charged you more as you improved, which is why they all died.

WHERE YOU SEE IT
Top line of every day card, and one notification at night: streak, levels this month, last night's verdict.

IF YOU SKIP THE LOGGING YOU DID NOT TRAIN, YOU JUST WORKED OUT.

THE ROLLOUT - NOTHING TURNS ON AT ONCE
Sep 1 to Sep 13. The Closer only. One number a day. Nothing else is logged and nothing is scored.
Sep 14 to Sep 27. Add the Good mark line. Still nothing is scored.
Sep 28. Add the bag missed line and the 50/50 racks line. The boxes, the verdict and the streak go live that Monday.
If the Closer log is not close to perfect on Sep 13, none of the rest gets switched on and we build a different kind of logging instead. That is the actual test, and it is cheap to fail.

new_pages.title: THE CLOSER
new_pages.body:
THE CLOSER

End of the morning block, every day, before you leave the gym. It took the morning passing slot. Passing moved to the afternoon, in front of the bag work. Nothing else was cut for it.

Never run it in the afternoon. A record needs the same conditions every time and the afternoon block ends tired.

One ball. Rebound your own. Clock starts on your first shot and stops on your twenty fifth make.

25 MAKES, IN THIS ORDER
8 one dribble pull up - 4 from the right elbow going right, 4 from the left elbow going left
8 reverse layup with the opposite hand - 4 each side, entering from the corner
4 deep three from the top of the key
5 free throws, last

Misses cost you seconds and so does standing around. That is the whole test. Shooting, finishing off both hands, range and free throws in about four minutes.

No constraints anywhere in it. This is a clean reference, the same job the reference layups do on Good Finishing. It is not a Good drill and it never gets a level.

LOG
One new line at the bottom, date and time, the second you stop the clock.
8/30 3:44

LAST 5
CLARVIS writes this line. Do not touch it.

Beat two of the last five and the Closer is beat. That is its own counter. It does not decide your day - a bad Closer can never cost you a win, because a record chase that can fail your day gets quietly abandoned.

THIS TEST NEVER CHANGES. If the times go flat for three weeks that is a finding for the monthly audit, not a reason to redesign it. The moment it changes, every time before it is worthless.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
It does not train transition. Transition's real gap is deciding, and a solo timed circuit cannot manufacture a decision. That is on Reps Transition and at Tuesday practice.

new_pages.title: GOOD DRILLS - HOW THEY WORK
new_pages.body:
GOOD DRILLS - HOW THEY WORK

WHAT A GOOD DRILL IS
Skill under constraint. Handling, shooting, finishing. Nothing else. Off ball, ball screen and team defense are positioning and decisions, not skills - they live in the bag rotation and at practice. Passing is not a Good drill either. There is one Passing page and it runs on blocks, not levels.

COMPOUND, NEVER ONE THING AT A TIME
A Good rep stacks constraints. Crawl start, spin, spin back, touch the backboard, adjust and finish coming down is off balance and max glass height and air adjustment and almost no perception time, in one rep. If a drill trains one idea at a time it belongs on a bag page.

WHAT YOU ARE TRAINING
Perception, balance and pace. Every ladder on every Good page is one of those three getting harder. Where a page lists its own targets, those are sub headings under these three, not a fourth idea.

NO MAKE STANDARDS ON A GOOD PAGE
Bag pages have make standards. 50/50 has make standards. Good pages do not, with one exception: the clean reference layups at the bottom of Good Finishing. That block is a check that the finish itself is still sound, not a Good drill. It is the only make count in the mode and it never gets a mark.

LEVELS
Every Good DRILL runs at its own level, written on its own line as NOW: L4. Levels are per drill, never per page. There is no generic ladder in this system - the ladder is printed under its own drill, and higher always means less time, worse position or more fatigue.

THE MARK - THIS IS THE WHOLE DAILY ASK
One new line at the bottom of the page. Today's date, then one character per drill, in the order they are printed above.
plus means clean, never on the edge, you could do it again cold
equals means on the edge, some reps held and some fell apart
minus means it broke down, you could not complete the constraint
dot means you did not run that one today
8/30 =+.-
That is the entire Good log. You never edit a NOW line, you never open a table, and a plus costs you nothing extra to type.

WHAT HAPPENS TO IT OVERNIGHT
A plus moves that drill up a level, and the NOW line is already rewritten when you walk in tomorrow. Two minuses in a row at the same level drops it one. Every move is written into LOG - Good Drills for you. You never remember yesterday's mark and you never have to.

AN ALL EQUALS DAY FAILS
If every drill you ran got an equals, you cruised, and the GOOD box does not pass. At least one plus or one minus. There is no way to record an easy day here. That is the point of the whole mode, and it is the answer to the thing you said about it not pushing you.

HOW MANY, AND WHICH
Two or three a session on Finishing and Handling. Shooting runs the page. Take the ones whose marks are oldest in the lines at the bottom of the page - the dots show you what you skipped last time.

MOVING UP AND DOWN
You do not decide this any more. The mark decides it, overnight, the same way every time. Do not talk yourself into a plus - it gets checked the next morning by a level you actually have to run.

THE 21 DAY RULE
Any drill whose level has not moved in 21 days is flagged on the monthly audit and gets bumped or replaced. No third option. A drill that has become a habit is not a Good drill any more.

new_pages.title: REPS - HOW TO RUN THEM
new_pages.body:
REPS - HOW TO RUN THEM

Bag pages groove game movements and they keep make standards. Good pages do not. Different job.

THE ONE RULE - NEVER TAKE THE SAME REP TWICE
Change the spot, the entry, the tempo, the depth, the angle. Same drill, different rep, every time.

TWO PASSES, NOT ONE BLOCK
Two attempts at a drill, then move to the next one. Down the list, then back through it.
Reps Off Ball and Passing run four passes, because their standards need four attempts a side. Those two pages say so at the top. Nothing else on any page overrides the number printed on that page.

THE BAR IS PER GATE AND IT DOES NOT CHANGE
3/4 ea side means 3 of 4 on that side, on that drill. It is never a page total. Varying the rep does not lower the bar.

EXCEPTION - TWO DRILLS RUN IN ONE BLOCK
Mistiming pull up, because it is a rhythm drill.
The clean reference layups on Good Finishing, because a reference needs clean conditions.
Those two by name. The exception is not keyed to a number, so nothing else falls into it when a standard changes.

FIRST WEEK ON A BRAND NEW PAGE
Block it to learn it, then interleave from week two. Every page in this rotation is new right now, so that means Sep 1 to Sep 7 and then never again.

THE MISSED LINE
Every drill on every bag page is numbered. The second you fail a drill's standard, put its number on today's line at the bottom of that page. Do not wait for the end of the block - you will not remember which of twelve it was three hours later, and a blank line reads as a clean day and tightens the pass line against you.
A clean day costs zero keystrokes. Blank means clean.
The pass line printed on each page is how many misses that day can carry. CLARVIS moves it: three clean days in a row and it drops one, two fails and it goes back up. You never work it out.

new_pages.title: REPS TRANSITION
new_pages.body:
REPS TRANSITION

Afternoon block, Monday, in the bag slot. The GET BACK block at the bottom runs in the Defense slot the same day and replaces the Defense page that day.

Run it varied, two passes. Never the same rep twice - change the side, the entry, the tempo, where you pick it up and how far out you start.

Full court. If you only have one basket, start every rep at the far three point line and treat that line as the far baseline.

The transition shots are already built. Full sprint into stop and Full sprint hard stop step back are on Bag Off Dribble. Transition full sprint is on Bag Shooting. Those days own the shot. This page owns everything around it.

This page grooves the movements. It does not train the read. The read is on Practice - Transition and Reads and it only gets tested Tuesday.

THE CUE
Before every GO rep, throw the ball off the glass hard and let it come off wherever it comes off. The side it comes off decides the lane you run. If it comes off long, past the free throw line, you have no advantage - run a PULL IT OUT rep instead of a GO rep. This is a real random cue, not a defender. Train it as reaction speed, not as a read.

THE RULE ON THIS PAGE
After every shot you take here, your first movement is a sprint back toward the far paint. Every rep, no exceptions. That is the habit this page is really buying. Same rule on the transition entries on Bag Off Dribble and Bag Shooting.

GO
1 Live board and go. Hard toss off the glass, rebound it in the air, chin it, rip to the open side, first dribble past the free throw line, sprint, finish far rim. 2/2 ea way
2 Long board, turn and push. Miss it long on purpose off the far side, chase it moving away from the rim, turn and push the other way in one motion, finish. 2/2 ea way
3 Outlet and beat it. Rebound, pivot on the outside foot, throw the outlet by rolling the ball hard up the sideline, sprint past it, pick it up on the run in the middle third, finish. 2/2 ea way

FINISH THE BREAK
4 Sprint lane, one foot. Full sprint the whole way, no stutter into the gather, finish off one foot on the run. 2/2 ea way
5 Sprint lane, two foot. Same sprint, gather on two feet inside the paint at full speed, finish off balance. 2/2 ea way
6 Wrong side pickup. Sprint, pick the ball up on the far side from the rim you are attacking, finish across the rim with the opposite hand. 2/2 ea way

PULL IT OUT
7 Pull out and re attack. Full sprint, decelerate under control above the break on two feet, one beat with your eyes up, then attack the same side before you drift. 2/3 ea way
8 Give it up and go get it. Full sprint, kill the dribble above the break, roll the ball out to the far corner, sprint after it, catch and shoot from that corner. 3/4 ea way

SECONDARY
9 Wide to the corner, then lift. Full sprint to the corner in your lane, plant, lift to the wing, catch and shoot. 3/4 ea way
10 Trail to the top. Sprint the trail lane, catch late at the top on the move, one motion three. 3/4 ea way

MISSED
Start today's line the second you miss one - date, then the number. Do not wait for the end of the block. Clear everything and you write nothing at all.
8/30 3, 7
PASS LINE: 2 or fewer
CLARVIS moves that number. Three clean days on this page and it drops one, two fails and it goes back up.

GET BACK - runs in the Defense slot, not in the bag slot
No makes in this block. Every rep is pass or fail and you know which one it was. Nothing here goes on the missed line.
Beat the ball back. From the offensive block, roll or throw the ball hard toward the far rim, then sprint to get into that paint before the ball does. 5 up, all 5 won. A lost one does not count.
Sprint back and locate. Sprint from the offensive corner to the nail, plant, turn, and call out loud what you see. Ball first, then the first man. 6 reps, out loud every time.
Match on the run. Set two markers, far wing and far corner. Sprint back, take the deepest one first, then jump to the ball marker. 6 reps. The markers are spots, not defenders. This is the footwork of getting matched and nothing else.

WHAT THIS PAGE CANNOT DO
Whether the advantage is real, who is actually ahead, when to give it up, and who to pick up. None of that reps alone, and a chair does not retreat or commit, so a chair rep would teach you to attack an advantage that is not there. It is on Practice - Transition and Reads and it only gets trained Tuesday.

new_pages.title: PRACTICE - TRANSITION AND READS
new_pages.body:
PRACTICE - TRANSITION AND READS

Read this before practice. Pick two. Not five, two. Score yourself out of 10 after, one row in LOG - Partner + Practice, Type is Intention.

This page exists because these are the things that cannot be repped alone. Reps Transition grooves the movement. This is where the deciding gets trained, and Tuesday is the only day it can happen.

TRANSITION OFFENSE
First look is up the floor on every rebound and every make, before the ball goes down. Count the possessions I looked first.
Push past the free throw line before I decide anything. No decision made above the arc.
Name the advantage to myself every break. Numbers, mismatch, or none. If none, pull it out on the first beat instead of driving into a set defense.
Every break ends one of three ways. I finish it, I hit the man ahead, or I pull it out clean. No dead dribble in the middle third.
When I am not the ball, I run wide to the corner every time. No drifting to the wing early.
As the trail man I am ready before the catch, and I shoot it in one motion if it is there.

TRANSITION DEFENSE
Paint first, man second. Get to the paint, then find who I have.
I take the most dangerous man, not my man, until we are matched up.
I talk on every get back. Call the ball, call who I have, out loud, every possession.
My first step after my own shot is back. Count the possessions I lost that step.

READING A CLOSEOUT
Three options on the catch and I decide on the catch, not before it. Shoot it. Attack the high shoulder. One more, and relocate.

BALL SCREEN, THE LATE READ
I do not decide before I leave. I read the coverage after the first dribble, not at the point of the screen. If I know the answer before I come off it, that was a bag rep, not a live one.
Hedge and blitz are the two coverages I have never repped anywhere. Those are the ones to go looking for at practice.

new_pages.title: OPEN QUESTIONS
new_pages.body:
OPEN QUESTIONS - NOT A TRAINING PAGE

Everything here was written to you as a reviewer, not as a player, and it was sitting on pages you read between reps holding a ball. It lives here now and the drill pages are back to being drill pages.

TWO DRILL LINES ARE STILL UNDEFINED. Only you can answer these.
Deep slides on Bag Ball Screen - what is that as a movement into the shot? Until you answer it, run it as a long lateral slide into the catch.
2 dribble pull up on Bag Ball Screen - two dribbles off which coverage? Until you answer it, run it off a drop.

DECISIONS ALREADY MADE, WRITTEN DOWN HERE SO THEY DO NOT GET RE ARGUED
Block stop hook layup sits at 2/2 because it is a rim finish off two feet at the block. Barkley middle bump hook stays at 3/4 because the bump is the skill there, not the finish. Those two are not the same call.
Bag off Screens was renamed Bag Ball Screen. It was always one hundred percent ball screen work. Off ball screen work is on Reps Off Ball and Bag Shooting.
Reps Passing was deleted. It was the same drill list as the Passing page under different names, and the day card only ever had one passing slot.
Good Off Ball, Good Ball Screen and Good Defense were deleted. They were marked reference only and their live content moved out first: the closeout read to Reps Off Ball and Practice - Transition and Reads, the ball screen late read to Practice - Transition and Reads, and start beaten to Court movement Defense Block C, which already had the same drill and the same progression.
Hedge and blitz are the only two ball screen coverages you have never repped. Switch, over the top and short roll all exist elsewhere in the program. That claim is stated once, here.
Vitamins stopped being a scored box. A box that always passes inflates a streak and tells you nothing.

IF YOU ANSWER ONE OF THESE, SAY SO AND IT GOES ON THE DRILL LINE ITSELF AND COMES OFF THIS PAGE.

cut_and_why: THE PLUS TAX - CUT. A plus no longer costs a mid-page NOW rewrite plus a four-cell table row. It is one character and CLARVIS does the rest overnight. The old design priced honesty about progress at roughly fifty times the price of drifting, in the exact block it claimed to be protecting, and then named all-equals drift as its only fatal failure mode. That was the whole problem.

PER-DRILL TODAY SLOTS - CUT. Six mid-page cursor placements in a wall of plain text, deleting yesterday's character first, is not four seconds a drill. Replaced by one append-only dated string at the bottom of the page. Design law now: he never edits an existing line anywhere in the app. Every line he touches is a new line at the bottom; every line CLARVIS maintains is machine-written.

VITAMINS AS A SCORED BOX - CUT. It had no in-page slot, so CLARVIS could not have written the Day cell from it, and a box that always passes inflates the streak and dilutes the verdict. It is now a printed prerequisite. Three boxes: GOOD, BAG, FINISH.

THE CLOSER BEAT AS THE DEFINITION OF A PERFECT DAY - CUT. As written, the highest status in the system was earned by shooting well on an unconstrained circuit, which pointed the whole status economy at his existing strength. P is now all three boxes plus a level moved today. Closer beats are a separate counter.

END-OF-BLOCK LOGGING - CUT, both places. Bag misses and 50/50 racks are now written at the instant they happen. Recalling which of twelve numbered drills failed across two varied passes after a four hour afternoon is a recall task wearing a logging costume, and the blank he would type reads as clean, ratchets the pass line to zero, and then starts failing his honest days. That sequence is how this ends.

THE MANUAL FALLBACK FOR THE DAY ROW - CUT. If the sync lags, the row gets written late. Nothing in LOG - Day, LOG - Week or LOG - Good Drills is his job under any condition. A thirty second fallback used twice a month is the 78-row table returning under a new name.

REPS PASSING - DELETED. Same drill list as the Passing page under different names, same equipment, same standard, word for word in places, and the day card only ever had one passing slot. Its unique deliveries fold into the Passing page.

GOOD OFF BALL, GOOD BALL SCREEN, GOOD DEFENSE - DELETED, not left as reference pages. They still carried levels, imperatives and a level number that does not exist. Live content moved first: the closeout read to Reps Off Ball, the ball screen late read to Practice - Transition and Reads, start beaten already existed on Court movement Defense Block C.

THE GENERIC L1-L7 LADDER on the Good rules page - CUT. Every real drill has its own ladder of its own length, so mid-session the rule page and the drill page told him two different things about NOW: L5.

THE OLD 50/50 LOG TABLE, 78 EMPTY ROWS - DELETED, not repurposed. Its data lives in the 50/50 cell of LOG - Day. Leaving a monument to a year of empty rows next to the new system is a standing argument that logging does not stick here.

BUILD COMMENTARY ON THE FOUR BAG PAGES - CUT to a single Open Questions page. Text addressed to him as a reviewer, including two unanswered questions sitting on live drills, was living on the pages he reads between reps holding a ball.

FREE THROWS TIRED as a Compete + Fatigue item - CUT. It demanded an all-day running tally of makes and attempts, which is exactly the arithmetic that will not happen, and contradicted 50/50's own sets-of-ten principle. It is a standing order on Vitamins now and is not logged.

THE 45 SECOND CLAIM - CUT and restated as thirty to forty seconds, four moments, none longer than twelve. The first time a claimed cost is visibly wrong is the first time he stops trusting the rest of the rulebook.

SHIPPING IT ALL ON DAY ONE - CUT. Five week rollout: Closer only for two weeks, then the Good mark line, then the bag and 50/50 lines and only then the verdict and the streak. Against a base rate of zero, a streak switched on in week one records nothing but failure and gets abandoned before it can pay.

morning_brief_for_alex:
Alex - the scoring layer is built, the transition gap is closed, and the library audit is applied. Read these five things first.

1. ONE THING HAS TO BE CHECKED BEFORE ANY OF THIS SHIPS. This whole design says you never fill in a table, and that rests on CLARVIS being able to WRITE INTO the training app - rewriting NOW lines on the three Good pages, LAST 5 on the Closer page, six PASS LINE numbers, and numbering the drill lines 1 to N on the six bag pages. Your PWA syncs into CLARVIS and CLARVIS is its backend, so I believe write-back exists, but I could not verify it from here. If it turns out to be read-only, all that page maintenance lands back on you and this becomes a bigger version of the 78-row table. Confirm write-back, then build. That is the one gate.

2. THE FIX TO YOUR ACTUAL COMPLAINT is one character a day. At the bottom of your Good page you type one line: 8/30 =+.- One character per drill. A plus means it was clean, and overnight that drill moves up a level and the page already says L5 when you walk in tomorrow. You never edit a NOW line and you never open a table. The earlier version of this charged you about a minute for typing a plus and one character for typing an equals - a fifty to one tax on admitting you got better, in the one block the whole thing exists to protect. That is gone. And an all-equals day now FAILS the day. You cannot cruise quietly any more, which is the actual answer to "it doesnt measurably push me every day."

3. THE ONLY THING SWITCHING ON SEP 1 IS THE CLOSER. One number, end of every morning, twenty five makes on a clock. Nothing else is logged and nothing is scored for two weeks. Sep 14 the Good mark line goes on. Sep 28 the bag and 50/50 lines go on and the streak starts. If the Closer log isn't near perfect on Sep 13 we don't switch the rest on - we build a version where CLARVIS asks you one question by notification at night instead. Given 78 empty rows, that is a cheap and honest test and it costs you nothing to fail.

4. TWO STRUCTURE CALLS I MADE THAT YOU CAN VETO. Tuesday's Upper System moves to the evening AFTER practice - Vitamins plus 26 working sets never fit in your 90 minute morning, and that squeeze was going to hand you a guaranteed lost day every single week. And Passing moves from the morning to the afternoon in front of the bag block, which is where the Closer's four minutes came from. Saturday Mobility moves to the afternoon lift slot for the same reason - it is honestly about 70 minutes, not the 46 the page claimed.

5. TRANSITION NOW HAS A HOME. Reps Transition runs Monday in the bag slot, the day before practice, and its GET BACK block takes Monday's Defense slot. Reps Passing came out of the bag rotation to make room - it was a duplicate of the Passing page anyway. The deciding half of transition is not solo-trainable and I did not pretend otherwise with chairs; it is on Practice - Transition and Reads and it gets tested Tuesday, same treatment off ball and ball screen already get.

Two things still need a word from you, both on Open Questions: what "deep slides" is as a movement into the shot, and which coverage the "2 dribble pull-up" comes off. Until you answer they run as a long lateral slide into the catch and off a drop.
